waypoints.name: Icicle Creek Road roadside parking (Hook Creek Drainage)
waypoints.note: Roadside parking used to access the Hook Creek Drainage spires above Icicle Creek.
waypoints.directions: From Leavenworth, take US-2 west to the edge of town and turn onto Icicle Creek Road. Follow it about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Forest Service Road 7601 and drive roughly 3.7 miles more to the Stuart Lake Trailhead. FR-7601 is a rough dirt road and high clearance is recommended.

waypoints.name: The Mole (Edward Peak) North Face topout
waypoints.note: USGS name for this formation is Edward Peak; North Face follows an obvious crack system, 5.7, with a 3-rappel descent to the east.

road.name: Icicle Creek Trailhead, Icicle Creek Road, Leavenworth
road.status: Icicle Creek Road itself is paved and well-maintained, but the final approach to the Icicle Creek Trailhead was washed out and closed (about 2 miles before the trailhead) with the closure expected to last until the end of 2026 — confirm current status before a trip.
road.driveNote: Roughly 2.5-3 hours from Seattle via US-2 to Leavenworth then Icicle Creek Road.

before.approach: Park at the Smithbrook Trailhead (elev. ~3,800 ft) on Smithbrook Road (FR 6700), about 2.7 miles up from Hwy 2. Start on the signed Smithbrook Trail (part of the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness trail system) and climb via nearly 20 short switchbacks, gaining about 650 ft in 1.2 miles to Union Gap on the PCT — Lichtenberg's summit is visible to the south for much of this stretch once the forest opens up. At Union Gap, turn left (south) onto the Pacific Crest Trail and follow it about 2 miles, contouring below Lichtenberg's east flank, to Lake Valhalla (~4,830 ft), passing through a mix of forest and open meadow/heather and crossing Smith Brook along the way (a reliable water source and a good place to filter before leaving the trail). From the north or east shore of Lake Valhalla, leave the PCT and begin the off-trail portion: contour and rising-traverse around the lake toward the peak's south/southwest side, picking through heather benches, boulder fields, and increasingly loose talus. There is no maintained trail above the lake — expect real route-finding, some bushwhacking through scattered subalpine fir, and a few short cliff bands that force minor backtracking; a GPS track or written beta is genuinely useful here. The standard line aims for a prominent gully on the south/southwest side of the summit tower (often snow-filled into early summer — an ice axe and sometimes light traction are worth carrying outside of peak summer), climbed as scree/talus with a bit of low third-class scrambling near the top to gain the final summit block. Total gain from the trailhead is roughly 2,000-2,500 ft over about 7 miles round trip, with 6-7 hours being a typical leisurely round-trip time.

waypoints.name: Smithbrook Trailhead
waypoints.note: End of FR 6700 gravel spur off US-2 near milepost 68; Northwest Forest Pass required, self-issue wilderness permit at the kiosk.
waypoints.directions: From US-2 near milepost 68, turn onto Smithbrook Road (FR 6700), a gravel spur, and follow it about 2.7 miles to the Smithbrook Trailhead at roughly 4,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and you self-issue the wilderness permit at the kiosk here. Smithbrook Road is unplowed in winter and typically melts out by early to mid summer; attempt it before the road opens and you add about two miles of snow-road walking each way.

waypoints.name: Smithbrook Trail / PCT junction
waypoints.note: Smithbrook Trail #1590 tops out at the Pacific Crest Trail; turn left (south) toward Lake Valhalla.

waypoints.name: Lake Valhalla, south tip
waypoints.note: Where the PCT bends southwest away from the lake, drop off-trail down a steep dirt path to the water and follow rocky shoreline to the south tip to leave the maintained trail.

waypoints.name: Base of southeast boulder slope
waypoints.note: Past the lake's south tip, boulder-hop southeast until Lichtenberg's southeast shoulder comes into view and a class 2 line up to the ridge is visible.

waypoints.name: Southeast gully / talus slope
waypoints.note: Loose rock and shifting talus on the class 2 climb to the ridgeline; test holds and watch for parties below.

waypoints.name: Ridge gain point west of true summit
waypoints.note: Boulder scramble tops out on the summit ridge just west of the true (east) summit; turn east for the final walk to the top.

waypoints.name: Lichtenberg Mountain summit
waypoints.note: True summit overlooks Lake Valhalla to the west and Lichtenwasser Lake to the northeast; on descent retrace the ridge and gully, taking care on the loose upper talus.

before.rope_note: No rope needed; Class 2 non-exposed scramble, 7mi/2100ft gain.
